verdict: Reddit's revenue grew 70% to $726M as ad sales jumped 75% — and with costs growing far more slowly, net income more than tripled to $252M, 35 cents of every revenue dollar.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads shown across Reddit's communities — powered by more users, more time on site, and better ad targeting.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Mostly data licensing — deals that let AI companies train on Reddit's public posts — plus Reddit Premium subscriptions.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the product and the ad platform — up 5% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning advertisers and users — up 103% YoY, the fastest-growing cost line.

takeaways.title: Growth accelerated
takeaways.text: Revenue growth hit 70%, powered by advertising (+75%) as daily users reached 121.4M, up 19% — Reddit is still getting bigger and better at selling ads against its communities.

takeaways.title: Profit more than tripled
takeaways.text: Net income rose from $71M a year ago to $252M — 35% of revenue. Costs grew far more slowly than revenue, so most of the new money dropped straight to the bottom line.

takeaways.title: Cash machine, now buying back stock
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $264M — 36% of revenue — and Reddit announced a $1B share buyback program alongside the results.

otherDetail: Other income of $23M, net — mostly interest earned on Reddit's cash and marketable securities.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to the nearest $M, following the same convention as Reddit's other pages; the statements report in thousands (total revenue $725.6M).
